title: Make standalone nrio look like Nova's built-in Rio by default
description:
Lucca, 2026-10-22, after launching standalone nrio (a6ba850c) with ~/.config/nrio/config.toml holding only [shell]: 'why does it look so bad' / 'lets fix the defaults' / 'it should be the same as the rio nova uses built in'. Today the Nova look lives only in Nova: defaults/rio/config.toml (decorations disabled, navigation plain, opacity 0.70 + blur + opacity-cells, JetBrains Mono 16 with Nerd symbol and Noto symbol-map, line-height 1.12, cursor #00e6ff, trail-cursor, adaptive-theme nova-dark/nova-light from defaults/rio/themes, panel margin/padding 0) with font dirs substituted by Nova's flake (jetbrainsMonoDir, symbolsNerdDir, notoSymbolsDir, notoEmojiDir). Standalone nrio deserializes the user file over upstream Config::default(), so missing keys get upstream Rio's look.

Decision: nova-rio owns the Nova terminal look. nrio embeds it as its base config and themes; the user's config.toml overlays it key by key (a [shell]-only file still gets the full look; user keys win). pkgRio.nix adds the fonts and fills additional-dirs at build; non-Nix builds fall back to installed fonts by family name. Coordinate with RIO-CONFIG-UI-001 (Ratconfig) and --write-config.

Loading entry points: rio-backend/src/config/mod.rs load(), try_load(), load_from_path (themes resolve from <config dir>/themes/<name>.toml; embedded nova themes need a fallback).

Acceptance: a [shell]-only nrio config renders like Nova's built-in Rio (same settings and themes); overlay unit tests (missing keys from base, user keys win, theme fallback); coexistence check still passes; private-display comparison against Nova's Rio (Kinestra recorder), then the owner's desktop. README delta list updated. Follow-up in Nova: consume this base and drop the duplicate defaults (Nova bead filed alongside).

title: Eliminate half-block banding with translucent cell backgrounds
description:
## Outcome and user impact

Remove artificial horizontal banding from standard half-block terminal artwork when window.opacity < 1 and window.opacity-cells = true. Nova users see this in Anima Aquarium as alternating dark/bright horizontal water rows; dense half-block animations such as Plasma, Chladni, and Physarum share the same rendering mechanism.

Consumer: any terminal application using foreground/background colors to represent two samples in a block character. Trigger: render equal-color upper/lower samples through Rio with explicit-background translucency enabled. Observable result: a flat source color must remain visually flat rather than alternating at half-cell height. Unequal source samples must retain their distinct colors and orientation.

Owner: Nova Rio's native cell color/compositing policy. Anima emits valid conventional Unicode/SGR output and should remain a standalone terminal animation library. This issue does not require changing animation palettes or adding Nova-specific behavior to Anima.

Classification: shared Linux/Darwin rendering behavior. Effort M; implementation risk MED; diagnosis confidence HIGH. Priority P2: confirmed visual defect, without demonstrated startup failure or data loss.

## Confirmed mechanism and exact source evidence

Baseline: Nova Rio 2ad2987d0580855393667651ce1d22f094901a23; upstream raphamorim/rio b2e7c38bdc56bb86b346ca4f37b9aeaa5151d790 (0.5.20). Installed Nova bea11dd7397690afeae99870d3a98b9cbbb498bc pins that Rio and Anima b3133f057fa0029b3e06c85301161168c48bb799.

- frontends/rioterm/src/grid_emit.rs:345-359, cell_fg: ordinary foreground colors retain their resolved opaque alpha.
- frontends/rioterm/src/grid_emit.rs:963-1038, cell_bg: explicit backgrounds receive renderer.cell_bg_alpha when opacity_cells is enabled; default backgrounds skip painting, while INVERSE retains an opaque-background exception.
- frontends/rioterm/src/renderer/mod.rs:85-90,160-162: opacity policy and precomputed round(window.opacity * 255) belong to Renderer.
- rio-backend/src/config/window.rs:192-201: native opacity-cells setting explicitly applies opacity to cell backgrounds; its native default is false.
- sugarloaf/src/sprite/block.rs:47-59: U+2580 upper half, U+2584 lower half, and U+2588 full block use built-in geometric coverage.
- sugarloaf/src/grid/shaders/grid_text.frag.glsl and grid_text.vert.glsl: text coverage/color is composited over the separately emitted cell background. Metal and WGPU have corresponding paths under sugarloaf/src/grid/shaders/.
- Anima src/lib.rs:196-224, HalfBlockField::render_lines: U+2580 uses the upper sample as foreground and lower sample as explicit background; U+2584 represents a lone lower sample.
- Anima src/aquarium.rs:239-255: water is a gradual vertical RGB gradient, without an alternating-row filter. Local Anima HEAD f704fef99683831b8b6242245b73e582d0caf3bf has identical renderer/animation source to Nova's pin.

Direct comparison of the three Rio files grid_emit.rs, sprite/block.rs, and config/window.rs against the upstream baseline found no fork delta. The relevant alpha behavior already exists upstream; do not describe this as a defect introduced by a Nova Rio patch. Nova's chosen opacity-cells=true exposes it.

## Reproduction and retained proof

Local proof directory:
 /home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/anima-horizontal-bands-20261009.wsu6gdky

Contains metadata.json, findings.txt, field.py, pixel-results.json, four native config directories, four PNG captures, and per-case logs. Screenshots were visually inspected.

Exact tested executable:
 /nix/store/dsg70anllcrqa5wfqvglb1aidjv8wpk4-nova-rio/bin/rio
Consumed by installed Nova:
 /nix/store/qzvmwrjbshpq1jar7cwrgbkjr4sizkq3-yazelix

The probe used a private Linux Xvfb display, the installed Rio, copied user font/line-height settings (JetBrains Mono 16, line-height=1.12), blur=false, a distinct purple default background, and constant equal foreground/background RGB=(40,100,160). It emitted the same character across every cell, bypassing both Nova and Zellij. All private windows and Xvfb stopped after capture; user config, profiles, and sessions were untouched.

Measured at x=100 over 300 rows:
1. U+2580, opacity=.70, opacity-cells=true: alternating RGB (66,72,115) and (56,99,155); visible stripes.
2. U+2580, opacity=.70, opacity-cells=false: one RGB color (56,99,155); flat.
3. U+2580, opacity=1.0, opacity-cells=true: one RGB color; flat.
4. U+2588, opacity=.70, opacity-cells=true: one RGB color; flat.
An assert-based comparison verified those outcomes.

The supplied Aquarium screenshot (/tmp/codex-clipboard-z26Sph.png) repeats bands every 12 pixels within 24-pixel terminal cells, matching the upper/lower half-block boundary. Blur is not required for this artifact. Keep raw measured RGB values as environment-specific evidence, not cross-platform expected literals.

To rerun a retained case in a separate test terminal, set RIO_CONFIG_HOME to its config directory and execute:
 RIO_CONFIG_HOME=/home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/anima-horizontal-bands-20261009.wsu6gdky/half-070-cells /nix/store/dsg70anllcrqa5wfqvglb1aidjv8wpk4-nova-rio/bin/rio -e /usr/bin/python3 /home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/anima-horizontal-bands-20261009.wsu6gdky/field.py '▀'
That command uses Nushell environment-assignment syntax. Replace the executable with the exact candidate package when proving a fix. If local files/store paths expire, reconstruct the same one-color fixture from the parameters above.

## Decision boundary and scope

Chosen goal: fix the inconsistent treatment in Rio while preserving ordinary text readability and Nova's existing 0.70 TUI-background transparency.

The user authorized implementation. Policy A below is selected from the native visual prototype and maintained fork size. Policy B is deferred because correct per-sample translucency requires coverage-aware compositing:
A. Keep explicitly colored half-block artwork opaque. This may fit the existing foreground-over-background model with the smallest isolated change.
B. Render both source samples uniformly translucent. Preserve real foreground/background separation and composite each sample exactly once.

Choose using installed visual evidence and maintained fork size. Do not claim that assigning alpha=.70 to both existing passes automatically implements B: foreground drawn over an already-translucent background can compound alpha and mix the background sample into the foreground sample. With two overlaid .70 layers, combined alpha is .91, not .70. A correct translucent implementation must account for coverage and existing layers.

Start with the confirmed U+2580/U+2584 + explicit-background case; prove full blocks as a control. Define the smallest affected glyph set from source evidence. Sparse half-blocks with default backgrounds must not gain an opaque rectangle. Do not automatically classify all box drawing, braille, quadrants, sextants, emoji, or terminal text as artwork, or generalize their behavior without a demonstrated need.

In scope: cell_fg/cell_bg routing and the native draw paths that actually need correction; focused renderer tests; a repeatable visual fixture; fork provenance/removal documentation for the final accepted patch.

Out of scope: Anima simulations/output schema, Zellij rendering policy, Nova default opacity, user config migration, a new public setting, alternate graphics backends, broad shader refactoring, new dependencies, unrelated fork cleanup, remote PR submission, channel promotion, or installing a trial into the user's active profile. Consuming a resulting child pin in Nova requires a separately authorized integration run.

## Implementation approach

1. Re-read current source and upstream at the subsystem above; reproduce the failure before editing. Refresh line references if source has changed. Record whether upstream already has an applicable correction.
2. Prototype the narrow opaque policy first if it satisfies the contract; compare uniformly translucent output only when it has a clear benefit. Record the accepted policy and explicitly rejected alternative. Keep one owner for opacity/coverage rather than independent per-animation or per-backend heuristics.
3. Add one strong regression around observable rendered samples/colors. Equal source colors must be uniform; unequal colors must remain correctly separated. Include reversed half-block orientation and ordinary text/background controls. A helper-alpha assertion alone cannot prove final compositing.
4. Cover explicit RGB and palette backgrounds, default-background sparse pixels, opacity=1, opacity-cells=false, INVERSE/selection/cursor exceptions, and odd/even cell heights within that bounded fixture or existing tests. Avoid one tiny test per literal.
5. Verify the exact packaged native renderer in a fresh terminal; visually inspect Aquarium plus one dense half-block field, with blur off and then the user's normal blur setting. Check normal Radar/sidebar and Nova Bar transparency/readability at .70.
6. Document the final fork delta and removal trigger. Do not modify upstream-owned code outside the accepted mechanism.

Dependency decision: no new crate, graphics protocol, service, or compatibility layer is justified. Reuse native cell/style data and existing procedural block coverage.

## Verification and completion boundary

Existing supported commands:
- cargo fmt -- --check --color always
- cargo test -p rioterm --features wgpu
- cargo test -p sugarloaf --features wgpu if Sugarloaf is changed
- nix build .#rio --no-link --print-build-logs
Run native-dependency commands in the repository's Nix development shell when host dependencies are unavailable (nix develop --command cargo test -p rioterm --features wgpu).

Expected success: relevant tests and package build pass, and the equal-color visual fixture has no periodic half-row color change while ordinary TUI cell transparency still works. Preserve controls and prove both upper/lower orientation, distinct samples, and no pixel gaps.

This is shared rendering: Linux Xvfb evidence alone does not establish Darwin Metal behavior. On 2026-10-09 the user explicitly clarified that Darwin proof is optional for this task, suggesting the Eon machine if available. No active Eon macOS server was available in the configured account, and Darwin is unclaimed. A future Nova integration must satisfy its exact-revision Linux CI, Darwin Package Smoke, installed launcher and fresh-session acceptance gates.

Current state: implemented with the opaque explicit-half-block policy. The exact native Linux package and fixed Aquarium/Plasma captures are verified. No Nova pin integration, active-profile installation, full Nova startup/handoff, Darwin acceptance or promotion is claimed. See the completion evidence and limits below.

## Stop conditions, related work, and upstream exit

Stop and report if the smallest correction changes general text opacity, forces default-background sparse pixels opaque, needs a new user setting/dependency, or requires a different product/platform policy. Reassess if current upstream no longer uses the cited mechanism. After two failures of the same validation mechanism despite a reasonable correction, retain the failure and hand off instead of adding production workarounds for the test environment.

Related Nova planning, read-only context:
- yazelix-5vl-rio-translucent-backgrounds-7lbb selected translucent TUI backgrounds (its historic .60 record predates the user's final .70 choice).
- yazelix-5vl-outlined-tabs-preview-r2k8 records the later .70 appearance work.
- yazelix-5vl-track-nova-fork-upstream-exit-m8kz.1 tracks Nova Rio's maintained deltas.
These are context, not blockers. No artificial cross-repository dependencies or extra issues are required.

Upstream relationship: generic terminal graphics/opacity correctness, potentially useful beyond Nova. Preserve an isolated, reviewable patch and reproducible upstream case. No external issue/PR submission is authorized here. Remove the local delta only when a released/pinned upstream equivalent satisfies the same rendering and normal-TUI controls on supported native paths.

## Implementation and completion evidence (2026-10-09)

The shared cell_bg Codepoint path keeps only explicitly colored U+2580/U+2584 backgrounds opaque, matching their already-opaque foreground samples. The default-background early return, ordinary text and inline background-only cells, inverse/selection precedence, and cursor shader overrides are unchanged. No shader, setting, dependency, Anima source or Nova configuration changed. README documents this tenth fork delta and its upstream removal trigger; misc/scripts/test-half-block-opacity.py is the repeatable visual fixture.

The compositing regression uses real row colors and procedural block coverage. It failed before the fix and passes afterward, covering equal/distinct RGB and palette samples, upper/lower orientation, full blocks, 23/24-pixel heights, inverse, selection, sparse default backgrounds, ordinary text/box/braille/quadrant controls, inline background-only colors, opacity=1 and opacity-cells=false. Complete rioterm WGPU suite: 180 passed. Native Nix package checks: 1,178 passed, 11 existing ignored. Formatting, Python syntax and diff checks pass.

Exact candidate: /nix/store/psnfxkg6g6d0wwnfnbbbav13qwq5l000-rio/bin/rio
Derivation: /nix/store/mama5cvjbd8i0wwnhhvdag4ajdfg2dr0-rio.drv
Binary SHA256: 5a3a75526900d965e60bd09c1e9c37fd57f16bab13c323d13cc0f52714f35f7c
Proof directory: /home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/rio-half-block-fix-20261009.Udcafc

Fresh private native Vulkan/Xvfb windows use the same VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES Mesa path as installed Nova's wrapper. Assert-based PNG checks prove one uniform 300-pixel equal-color column instead of the baseline's alternating pair, RGB/palette flatness, distinct orientation with no gaps at actual 23/24-pixel heights, full-opacity/no-cell-alpha controls, and pixel-identical ordinary TUI, inverse, sparse and selected regions. Aquarium and Plasma were visually inspected with blur=false and blur=true. Xvfb has no desktop blur compositor, so blur=true proves the requested native configuration rather than the desktop effect. Raw RGB values are local measurements, not portable literals.

Normal TUI transparency is proven by unchanged cell routing, the compositing regression and pixel-identical native ordinary-text/space controls. Source inspection found no affected U+2580/U+2584 output in the Bar/Radar renderers. Standalone live Radar/Bar capture exited twice and was stopped under the validation stop condition; live product-layout readability is not claimed. Cursor override ordering was source-reviewed; a visible native cursor proof was not established. Full Nova integration remains separate.

Failed unwrapped debug captures (dev-shell glibc/Xvfb mismatch and missing host xkbcommon-X11) and initial direct-package capture without Nova's Mesa environment are retained with logs. No production workaround was added for these test environments. metadata.json, candidate.patch, pixel-check.py/pixel-results.json, fixture copy, package/test logs and screenshots retain the exact evidence.

Upstream main 59203ccd5fa1e6b760a738c1ad653bb29f2f3465 is 102 commits beyond b2e7c38. Its emitter moved to rio-grid but retains the mismatched alpha routing; affected native shaders have no correction. An update alone does not fix this issue. Upstream 574f120b fixes dim/bold recoloring of backgrounds and 35728163 fixes Windows premultiplied transparency; neither fixes this Linux half-block case. Other useful update material includes PTY lifecycle, cursor trails, synchronized updates, Kitty placeholders and CoreText font-face fixes. The user agreed to this isolated correction and a separate future fork update. No unrelated cherry-pick or remote submission was made.
design: Accepted: opaque explicit backgrounds only on U+2580/U+2584, matching the existing opaque foreground and preserving source samples. Terminal-default backgrounds still skip painting, so sparse halves do not gain rectangles. Ordinary text and background-only encodings retain configured opacity. Rejected: making both existing layered passes translucent, which compounds alpha and mixes samples; true uniform translucency needs coverage-aware compositing and a larger fork delta. Keep correction at shared cell color emission, with no backend-specific or Anima-specific logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal-color explicitly colored U+2580 and U+2584 artwork has no artificial alternating half-row bands at opacity=.70 with opacity-cells=true; distinct samples retain correct colors and orientation.
- The selected artwork opacity policy and affected glyph set are recorded from a visual prototype; normal text/Radar/Nova Bar backgrounds preserve their .70 translucency and readable foregrounds.
- Default-background sparse pixels, opacity=1, opacity-cells=false, palette/RGB colors, selection/INVERSE/cursors, and odd/even cell heights retain intended behavior.
- A focused compositing regression fails on the baseline and passes on the candidate; exact packaged fresh-terminal captures support the rendering claim.
- Exact packaged native Linux evidence is complete for this fix; Darwin evidence is distinguished and optional per the user's 2026-10-09 clarification. Shared-platform acceptance and Nova integration/promotion are separately authorized.
- The patch adds no new setting/dependency or Anima-specific workaround, and its upstream provenance/removal trigger is documented.
notes:
Implemented policy A and verified the exact native Linux package. All compositing/pixel assertions pass; 180 rioterm WGPU tests and 1,178 native Nix package tests pass (11 existing ignored). Proof, package identity, patch, fixture, screenshots and failed-environment logs: /home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/rio-half-block-fix-20261009.Udcafc.
User authorized implementation and clarified native Darwin proof is optional; no active Eon macOS machine was available. Current upstream 59203ccd still has the bug; user agreed to isolated correction rather than a broad fork update.
Limits: no Darwin Metal or desktop compositor blur proof; live standalone Radar/Bar captures failed twice and were stopped, while ordinary TUI native controls remain pixel-identical and Bar/Radar source does not emit the affected glyphs. Cursor override source is unchanged; no visible-cursor capture established. No Nova pin/profile installation, full launcher acceptance, promotion, commit/push, upstream PR, new setting or dependency.

Bounded fresh-eyes/simplification pass (2026-10-09): fixed visual fixture exact-fit last-row omission and synchronized-update cleanup on interruption. Expected source colors are resolved together and independently of observed foreground output; deliberate wrong-foreground mutation now fails. Full rioterm WGPU suite passes (180), fixture boundary/interruption/output checks pass, formatting/diff pass. Rendering function unchanged apart from explanatory comment. Review ledger and proof: /home/lucca/.local/state/codex/proofs/rio-half-block-fix-20261009.Udcafc/bounded-review. No native package rebuild for test/comments/fixture/docs-only edits; previous native rendering evidence and platform/live-product limits remain unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented the narrow opaque explicit-half-block policy; baseline-failing compositing regression, full tests and exact native Linux package pixel/Anima captures pass. Upstream still has the bug. User made Darwin optional; validation limits and stopped live Radar/Bar captures are documented.

title: Open standalone nrio on non-NixOS Linux desktops
description:
Lucca, 2026-10-22: after 'nix profile add github:Yazelix/nova-rio/edge#nrio' (aead5c08) on Pop!_OS (hybrid Intel/NVIDIA), launching Nova Rio: 'mine wont open lol'. The standalone package links the Nix Vulkan loader but ships no driver manifests; Nova's full package already wraps nrio with --set-default VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES <mesa>/share/vulkan/icd.d (Nova bead yazelix-5vl-otmd: additive discovery keeps host NVIDIA; VK_ICD_FILENAMES was rejected because it hid nvidia_icd; an explicit user VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES, VK_DRIVER_FILES or VK_ICD_FILENAMES keeps Vulkan Loader precedence).

Contract: on Linux, bin/nrio is a wrapper that sets a default VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES to the packaged Mesa manifest directory; Darwin is unchanged.

Acceptance: coexistence check asserts the Linux wrapper sets VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES and never VK_ICD_FILENAMES; package builds; the owner's nix profile install opens Nova Rio from the desktop. Follow-up after Nova pins this: Nova's own wrapper becomes a duplicate owner.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Implemented from base aead5c08: pkgRio.nix wraps bin/nrio on Linux with --set-default VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES <mesa>/share/vulkan/icd.d (same mechanism as Nova's wrapper, bead yazelix-5vl-otmd); Darwin unchanged. check-coexistence.sh asserts the wrapper sets VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES and never VK_ICD_FILENAMES (reviewer seeded VK_ICD_FILENAMES into a scratch copy: check exits 1). Proof: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.coexistence .#nrio passed (nrio /nix/store/8dlsxkzmxd3b6aabx7c6fy1h3r8iwvy5-nova-rio). Private Xvfb :97 launch, isolated config, no Vulkan env: aead5c08 nrio panicked 'vkCreateInstance failed ... ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER' (0 Mesa manifests); candidate stayed up 8 s with 27 Mesa manifests and nvidia_icd still found. Converge: one fresh Claude round, README-only fix accepted. Note: any misc/ change alters nrio's source and forces a full Rust rebuild. Remaining: owner's desktop launch after nix profile upgrade; then Nova can drop its duplicate wrapper once it pins this revision.
